explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly validates LLM-based evaluation metrics against human evaluation results through correlation analysis on the same 100 dialogue sessions from the test set

prompts.notes: Detailed prompt templates provided in figures (Figure 13, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22) showing scoring criteria and evaluation processes for different metrics

inter_annotator_agreement.interpretation: High consistency observed for StiGQ, Es, Flu, Inf; moderate for Et and Con; poor for StiD

guidelines.notes: Complete human evaluation questionnaire with detailed description and scoring criteria for each metric provided in appendix (Figure 14)

sample_size.notes: Validation performed on 100 dialogue sessions randomly selected from STICKERCONV test set, evaluated by both LLM and human evaluators

quantitative_scores.notes: Correlation between LLM CON metric and human Con metric

validation_results.summary_finding: LLM-based metrics show strong correlation with human evaluations (Spearman: 0.87-0.90, Kendall: 0.74-0.80), demonstrating that with carefully designed prompts, LLM can effectively evaluate empathy tasks and align with human perceptions

criteria_mapping.notes: LLM Rank metric corresponds to average of all human scores; f-MMr corresponds to average of multiple human metrics (Con, Flu, Inf, StiD)
